title: Practice 6: с-: down, and together — раз-: apart

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Я к начальству ___ (снести / сносить — to carry down)!.
exercises.why: Antonym: вз- — После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. — с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.. **с-, со- (+сь, +ся)** — Convergent movement from various directions towards one center. — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0)  ·  From Антон Чехов, «Верба».
exercises.context: Antonym: вз- — После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. — с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst..

exercises.q: Вы меня с ума ___ (свести / сводить — to lead, to take)!
exercises.why: The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  From Александр Островский, «Бедность не порок».
exercises.context: The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы.

exercises.q: Вы с ума меня ___ (свести / сводить — to lead, to take).
exercises.why: **свести́** — **своди́ть** — to lead, to take (from somewhere); to bring together, to throw together. **свезти́** — **свози́ть** — (perfective only, transitive) to transport, to drive, to convey; (colloquial, perfective only, transitive) to transport there and back, to drive there and back. **сле́зть** — **слеза́ть** — to come down, to get down (from), to dismount (from); (colloquial) to come down. **сойти́сь** — **сходи́ться** — to meet, to come together; to converge, to coalesce. — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  From Александр Куприн, «Юнкера».
exercises.context: свести́** — **своди́ть — to lead, to take (from somewhere); to bring together, to throw together.

exercises.q: Понемногу все ___ (расползаться — to crawl away) из комнаты.
exercises.why: The second actor (if mentioned) is always in the Instrumental case with the preposition "**с**": *Я не хочу встречаться с этим человеком.* Note that without "**-ся**" the verb **встречать** — **встретить** is used with the direct object in the Accusative case: *Вчера я встретил моего друга.* but: *Мы встретились на улице.* We already know that the verbs in "**-ся**" may be divided into several groups. Verbs which never occur without the ending "**-ся**": *Я боюсь вашего брата.* — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 66–67.  ·  From Александр Куприн, «Яма».
exercises.context: The second actor (if mentioned) is always in the Instrumental case with the preposition "**с**": *Я не хочу встречаться с этим человеком.* Note that without "**-ся**" the verb **встречать** — **встретить** is used with the direct object in the Accusative…
